classification.habitat: Cultivated and naturalized in temperate to subtropical regions; commonly grown as a culinary and medicinal crop
classification.distribution: Widely cultivated in India and elsewhere

identification.description: Small aromatic annual herb with finely divided leaves and characteristic compound umbels.
identification.whole_plant: Erect, branched aromatic annual herb, generally about 20–60 cm tall.
identification.stem: Slender, branched and green; upper branches bear the inflorescences.
identification.leaf: Lower leaves broader and more divided; upper leaves finely dissected into narrow segments.
identification.flower: Small white to pinkish flowers arranged in compound umbels.
identification.fruit: Dry globose to ovoid schizocarp, commonly called coriander seed; aromatic when crushed.
identification.seed: Two mericarps remain closely joined in the mature fruit; surface shows characteristic ridges.
identification.bark: Not applicable as a distinct medicinal bark drug.
identification_points: Compound umbels with small pale flowers
Marked difference between lower and upper leaf division

modern_information.evidence_summary: Coriander is an aromatic culinary and medicinal plant. Its fruits and essential oil contain volatile constituents, with linalool commonly reported as a major component.
modern_information.safety_notes: Use correctly identified plant material. Avoid presenting traditional indications as established clinical efficacy.

student.quick_revision: Dhanyaka (Coriandrum sativum) is an aromatic Apiaceae herb; the characteristic medicinal part is the dry fruit.

teaching_points: Differentiate the lower and upper leaf forms.
Demonstrate the compound umbel and schizocarp fruit.
Relate botanical fruit terminology to the commonly used term coriander seed.
discussion_points: Authentication of dried fruit by aroma and morphology
practical_points: Observe whole herb and dried fruit separately.
Crush the fruit to demonstrate characteristic aroma.
Record colour, size, ridges and odour of authenticated sample.

doctor.quick_reference: Dhanyaka — Coriandrum sativum L.; Apiaceae; commonly used part: fruit. Traditional indications in the indexed record include Trishna, Daha, Jwara, Mutrakrichha and Ajeerna.
key_precautions: Do not infer patient-specific dosing from this educational record.
Separate traditional indications from modern clinical evidence.
